findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Not done.
Case: normal use - an agent removes the generated tools import but leaves its registration call. The retained module is scanned only for imports, so `register_tools()` is missed and the check can report all clear. The generated entry at `src/forge/templates/starter-python/apps/api/app/projects/__init__.py:7` calls that function on line 9; after its import is removed, the retained database setup's import at `apps/api/migrations/env.py:9` fails with `NameError`. The command should identify the remaining initialization before declaring success.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Functional.
Case: normal use - manual removal deletes the model class but leaves `models.py` with a schema constant or comment containing `"people"`. This test treats that text alone as a data model, so the check can print all clear even though the retained table is absent from SQLAlchemy metadata and Alembic's model check will see drift. The file's existence and a quoted schema name do not establish that a model remains.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done.
Case: normal use - a jobs module uses clients through `from app import clients`, `from ..clients import ClientService`, or `fetch(`${API_BASE}/clients`)`. The Python import pattern at line 57 accepts only `import app.clients` or `from app.clients`, and this URL pattern accepts only a full `/api/v1/clients` or a slash immediately following a quote. None of those valid uses is named, so the agent can remove clients without being warned that jobs depends on it.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done.
Case: normal use - a React Router app uses relative paths such as `<Route path="people" element={<PeoplePage />} />` and `<Link to="people">People</Link>`. Neither line contains a slash-prefixed route or one of the recognized module class names. A page imported from `./pages/people` is missed as well, so after the other references are removed the check can report all clear while the screen and navigation remain.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done.
Case: normal use - a Python demo loader adds records with SQLAlchemy, for example `session.add(Person(name="Ada"))`. Python never collects model names, and the sample-data patterns recognize only raw `INSERT INTO` statements and TypeScript Prisma accessors. The related `from app.people.models import Person` is listed, but the insertion is not; removing the listed import can therefore leave a broken loader while the check reports all clear. The starter itself uses model construction and `db.add` in `src/forge/templates/starter-python/apps/api/app/projects/service.py:285`.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done.
Case: normal use - a manually extended invoices feature has an `invoices.approve` permission or an `invoices_approve` agent tool. The access-rule pattern recognizes only five fixed actions, and the tool pattern on line 54 recognizes only six. A surviving permission check or test for the custom action is invisible and can remain after an all-clear. The Python starter's permission registry accepts role action strings at `src/forge/templates/starter-python/apps/api/app/core/permissions.py:25`.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done.
Case: normal use - a team removes the starter's projects feature. Both starters have tests referring to its MCP resources, including `app://projects/fields`; see `src/forge/templates/starter/apps/api/test/mcp.e2e-spec.ts:174` and `src/forge/templates/starter-python/apps/api/tests/test_mcp.py:234`. None of the patterns matches these resource URIs. The check can therefore miss assertions that will fail once the resource is removed, including after the recognized tool references have been cleaned up.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional.
Case: normal use - jobs was generated with a link to clients, and manual cleanup removes its imports and package dependency but misses the project reference. `src/forge/feature.py:147` generates `../../clients/contracts` in `libs/jobs/server/tsconfig.json`; this pattern requires `libs/clients/` or an `@app/clients-...` package name, so the reference is not listed. Once `libs/clients` is removed, the check can pass despite a dangling TypeScript project reference that breaks typechecking.
findings.title: Functional: Detect generated TypeScript project references

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done.
Case: normal use - a jobs file has an inline comment such as `value = 1  # see /api/v1/clients`, or an API documentation field with `example: '/clients'`. Both lines pass the leading-comment check and are classified as uses by jobs. The command then tells the agent that jobs depends on clients and to ask which feature to change first, even when these are only comments or examples.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done.
Case: normal use - a growing Python app has a generated `libs/shared/api-types/openapi.json` larger than 1 MB. The check silently skips the entire file, so a stale `/api/v1/people` route in it is neither listed nor prevents an all-clear. This is a file the branch explicitly checks for route leftovers at `tests/test_feature_remove.py:307`; the size limit creates an unreported exception to that behavior.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Test.
Case: normal use - a regression makes a successful check write a new, untracked migration. `git diff --name-status` and the subsequent diff omit untracked files, while the command skips migration directories during its scan, so this test can still pass. The successful command calls also have no before-and-after status assertion elsewhere in the new tests. The test does not establish the promised read-only behavior or that no new migration is written.
